newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ATHLETICS-TRASON WINS SECOND COMRADES IN A ROW.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-TRASON WINS SECOND COMRADES IN A ROW.

text.p: America's Ann Trason won her second Comrades ultra marathon women's title in a row when she overtook Germany's Maria Bak in the last six kilometres on Monday.
Trason, widely regarded as the world's best women's ultra marathon runner and winner of the 1995 world 100km championship, became only the second woman to finish the event in under six hours.
Her time of five hours, 58 minutes and 27 seconds over the gruelling course from Pietermaritzburg to Durban is second only to South African Frith Agliotti's record time of 5:54:43 in 1989.
"I never thought I would break six hours in this race - that puts me in the same orbit as Frith Agliotti. It's just amazing!" Trason said.
Trason, who suffered from stomach trouble during her run, trailed Bak by two minutes for much of the race.
But Bak, the 1995 champion, slowed in the closing stages because of a heel injury and finished in 6:00:27.
Russia's Valentina Liakhova was third with a time of 6:22:58.
Leading times in the women's marathon (South African unless stated):
1. Ann Trason (U.S.) five hours 58 minutes 27 seconds
